title: Find why the steward's decisions source is empty and fix or document it
summary: The steward's `decisions` source (defined in crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs) reported empty. The job finds the cause, writes it down, and makes decisions readable to the steward, or records why it cannot be. Audience: the steward and the maintainer reading its introspections.

defaults_applied.how: A test covers the decisions source behavior; cargo test and clippy must be clean.
The job finds why the source is empty rather than only silencing the message.
The criterion runs a test that shows the decisions source populated, not just a wiring check.
The check is the steward being able to read decisions, or a recorded reason it cannot.
A verifier runs fmt, clippy and test.
One focused change on the decisions source.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs (SOURCES lists `decisions` with two record directories; GitView::workspace writes every file from RecordSet::load, then creates any missing source directory as empty), crates/athena-gate/src/records.rs (RecordSet::load copies every blob under records/ at HEAD after check_record_file), crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (AnyRecord paths for decision-state and default-expectations records; round-trip tests around lines 3372 and 3405), crates/athena-core/src/store.rs (Records::load). Order: load records at HEAD, write files, then mkdir missing source dirs, so an empty source means nothing is committed under those paths at HEAD, not a copy bug.

Those two record directories do not exist in the snapshot I read (records/ is hidden from readers by design), so I could not confirm directly that no decision records are committed. Working hypothesis: no decision-state or default-expectations records are committed at the base commit (they are written but not landed, or D84 lives in docs/design only). The producer must verify this with git log/show on the record paths and with Grep over crates/ for the writers (Athena::record_default_expectations, decision-state writer) before choosing a fix.

If the cause is a missing writer or an unlanded record, the fix is in code (steward workspace or the writer). If decisions are legitimately empty, the fix is to make the steward's empty-source message say so and to record that in docs. No new record file is added under crates/, so no AnyRecord change is expected.
The user's stated outcome is the goal: reading decisions works or the notes say why not. The cause note goes in CHANGELOG.md and, if useful, docs/records.md.

acceptance_criteria.text: The change writes down the cause of the empty `decisions` source in a committed file (CHANGELOG.md or docs/records.md), citing the code path (crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs and crates/athena-gate/src/records.rs) that produces the empty directory. A reader can check this with git diff.

Either the diff changes crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs (or the record writer) so the steward's workspace holds decision records when they exist at HEAD, with a test in the same crate that builds a view containing a decision-state record and asserts the file appears under the decisions source paths, or the committed notes state why decisions cannot be read and what would change that.
A test that the decisions source is populated when a decision-state record exists in the view and stays an empty directory when none exists; run `cargo test -p athena-core steward` and it passes.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass on the change.
No file under records/ is edited, and no governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml) is changed.

out_of_scope: Editing or fabricating files under records/
Redesigning the other steward sources (jobs, events, introspections, class-registry, git-log, code)
Changing the decision-state or default-expectations record schemas
departures: The cause is unconfirmed because records/ is hidden from the reader, so there is more risk that the fix turns out to be notes only and the verifier judges it differently.
